segments.summary: Watson's framing preamble about the Holmes case archive and the year '87, introducing the remarkable case to follow.
On a stormy September night at Baker Street, John Openshaw recounts the K.K.K. orange-pip deaths; Holmes advises action and deduces the Ku Klux Klan is behind it.
Next morning at breakfast, news arrives of Openshaw's death. Holmes, shaken and prideful, resolves to hunt the gang himself.
That evening Holmes returns having traced the murderers to the barque Lone Star; he sends pips and alerts police, but the ship is lost at sea before justice is served.

The next morning Holmes learns from the newspaper that Openshaw has been killed; deeply shaken, he resolves to hunt down the gang himself.
